# Intake brief — Full-suite runs dirty the main checkout ship-config.csv

> **Source request (verbatim):** "Full-suite test runs (observed with
> changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leave
> src/data/ship-config.csv modified in the MAIN checkout
> (thrustAcceleration/maxSpeed/frictionDeceleration/controlScheme changes),
> even though the suite runs from a worktree. A test exercising
> GymPlayer.saveShipConfig writes through the dev-server CSV plugin whose root
> resolves to the main checkout (likely via the symlinked node_modules / vite
> project root). This trips the implement dirty-tree gate on later sessions,
> requiring a git checkout restore; it can also silently clobber an operator's
> tuned ship config. … add a guard so suites never write the repo's tracked
> CSV."

## Headline

Full-suite test runs leak writes to the tracked `src/data/ship-config.csv` in the **main checkout** even when the suite runs from a worktree, breaking the implement dirty-tree gate and risking silent clobbering of an operator-tuned ship config. Fix the dev-server CSV plugin's root resolution and add a guard so suites never write a tracked repository CSV.

## Problem statement

Running the full test suite (observed during changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leaves `src/data/ship-config.csv` modified in the MAIN checkout — `thrustAcceleration`/`maxSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration`/`controlScheme` diverge from the committed values — despite the suite having run from a worktree. The only writer of the tracked CSVs is the dev-server CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`): its write handler resolves `resolve(root, 'src/data/ship-config.csv')` where `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274), and the config store's dev-mode save (`saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves`, gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV`, which is `true` under vitest) issues a **relative** `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (`src/core/configStore.ts` lines 397–405, 569–586). In vitest's happy-dom integration project (default `window.location` = `http://localhost:3000`, verified in the installed vitest source), happy-dom's fetch resolves relative URLs against that origin — so a real (un-mocked) save PUTs to `http://localhost:3000/api/csv/...`; whatever server answers there can write through a root that points at the main checkout. Worktrees symlink `node_modules` to the main checkout (confirmed on four live worktrees), which lets Vite's project-root/package-root inference escape to the main checkout. The worktree's own `csv-seed.test.ts` reads its CSVs via `__dirname`, so a leaked write to the *other* checkout is not caught by the seed tests in the active checkout. Consequences: the implement dirty-tree gate fails on later sessions (manual `git checkout` restore required), and an operator-tuned ship config can be silently clobbered; it likely also explains intermittent `csv-seed` / `<suite exited 1>` smoke failures (AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL, AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP, AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2).

## Users

- **Developers / AI agents running the suite** — "As a developer I want suite runs to never modify tracked config files in any checkout, so the implement dirty-tree gate stays green and I don't have to restore files manually."
- **Designers/operators tuning ship config** — "As a designer I want my tuned `ship-config.csv` to survive test runs, so my balance work isn't silently overwritten."
- **Test suite maintainers** — "As a test author I want tests to exercise save behaviour against isolated fixtures, so the suite is deterministic and hermetic."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No tracked-file writes from suites** — Running the audit-accepted full suite (`npm --silent test`: `unit` + `integration` projects) from a worktree leaves every tracked `src/data/*.csv` (`ship-config.csv`, `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`) unchanged in **both** the active worktree and the main checkout. Verified by an automated pre/post `git status --porcelain` of both checkouts that runs as part of the change's tests (a regression guard the suite itself asserts).
2. **Root isolation in the plugin** — The CSV plugin never resolves write targets to a checkout other than the active project root: the implicit `process.cwd()` default is replaced by an explicit, verified root (derived from the Vite-resolved root, or an explicit option), and any request whose resolved target escapes the active root is refused with no file I/O (HTTP error + logged reason). Existing explicit-root test fixtures keep working unchanged.
3. **Test-mode write guard in the store** — Under the vitest/test harness (`import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'` detected in `configStore.ts`), `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` must never write a tracked repository file: they either update the registry only (documented no-op wrt disk, preserving registry semantics used by tests) or route writes to an isolated temp fixture. A direct unit test covers each save function under test mode asserting no file on disk changes.
4. **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. Add a comment in the integration tests documenting the relative-fetch/bridge pattern and verifying the bridge is installed for every real save.
5. **Documentation and full suite** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (plugin root semantics, test-mode guard and store save behaviour) and any relevant wiki/docs entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and the existing seed/validation tests (`csv-seed.test.ts`, `configStore.*`, plugin tests, gym save tests) remain green.

## Constraints

- Dev-only behaviour is preserved: while `npm run dev` runs from the active checkout, gym Save/Save As must still persist through the plugin to the committed CSVs (read-write dev workflow, AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA). Production builds stay read-only (`apply: 'serve'`).
- Atomic-write semantics (temp file + rename) and the post-save registry re-read (`reReadRegistry`) must be preserved on the success path.
- Test isolation is a requirement, not an option: current unit/integration tests already pin temp fixtures via explicit `root`; the gap is the default path and the dev-mode relative fetch. Do not weaken existing fixture patterns.
- Worktree isolation rules apply: implementation happens in a worktree; the main checkout is never edited directly.
- UK English for prose/comments; Markdown for work-item and code-doc prose.

## Existing state

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — `configCsvPlugin(options)`: `const root = options.root ?? process.cwd();` (line 274); `handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath), …)` for ship/enemy/difficulty CSVs. Registered in `vite.config.ts` with no options (`configCsvPlugin()`, so default root = `process.cwd()` of the dev server / test process).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isDev()` = `import.meta.env.DEV === true` (line 97); `fetchCsv`/`putCsv` use relative `/api/csv/...` URLs (lines 397–405, 569–586); `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` (lines ~612–660) gate only on `isDev()`.
- Vitest config (`vitest.config.ts`) — `unit` (node) and `integration` (happy-dom, default origin `http://localhost:3000`) projects; `isolate: true`; the full suite is `unit` + `integration`.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` (lines 80, 121–133) and `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — real plugin behind an ephemeral HTTP server against a **temp** root with an explicit fetch bridge; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts` / `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — `vi.mock('../../core/configStore')` replacing `saveShipConfig` with an in-process registry seed; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — reads CSVs via `__dirname`, i.e. relative to the **active** checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it.
- Worktree layout — `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with `node_modules` symlinked to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed on four live worktrees: wl-AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40-*, wl-AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V-*, wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q-*, wl-AH-0MVNT27XR0080I3C-*).

## Desired change

1. Make the plugin's write root explicit and safe: derive it from the Vite server's resolved project root (with an explicit override option), and refuse any write whose target resolves outside the active root. This removes the unpredictable `process.cwd()` default.
2. Add a store-level test-mode guard so the vitest harness can never write tracked files (registry-only no-op or temp-fixture routing), closing the relative-fetch escape route at the source.
3. Harden regression coverage: a suite-run cleanliness assertion (pre/post `git status` on both checkouts) plus unit tests for the new root guard and the test-mode guard.
4. Document the safe patterns (explicit roots, fetch bridges, module mocks) alongside the plugin and store modules.

## Key Files

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — replace the `process.cwd()` default root with an explicit/Vite-resolved root that is verified against the active checkout; add the escape-refusal guard; update `ConfigCsvPluginOptions` docs.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — tests for default-root behaviour (must not write outside active root) and the escape-refusal guard.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — add test-mode detection to `isDev()`/save guards; document relative-fetch + bridge pattern.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` / `configStore.integration.test.ts` — tests for test-mode save no-op/temp routing; fixture pattern comments.
- `vite.config.ts` — pass an explicit root derived from `server.config.root` if the plugin cannot self-derive it.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — optionally extend the seed check to also assert a clean worktree/main-checkout diff (the suite-run cleanliness guard may live here or in a new small test).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` (only if behaviour changes; otherwise untouched) — `_onSave` consumes `saveShipConfig`'s `ok/reason`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole": where the leak was first observed (`discovered-from`).
- **AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL** — "[test-failure] csv-seed.test.ts / configStore.integration.test.ts — ship-config.csv diverges from DEFAULT_CONFIG": the smoke symptom of a leaked write (`thrustAcceleration 390` vs `300`).
- **AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT** — "enemy-configs.csv working-tree change removes header and trailing newline (fails csv-seed tests)": sibling symptom on the enemy CSV.
- **AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP**, **AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2** — "[test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test": possibly same intermittent root cause.
- **AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA** (config-store epic), **AH-0MUE2MHRC0090AXP** (CSV plugin), **AH-0MUE2MIK9001TK88** (integration tests) — origin of the dev write-back design being hardened here.
- **AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V** — "Ship config controlScheme does not survive game server restart": dev-server persistence semantics for ship config.
- **AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4** — "Gym config save strips the CSV comment header block": another save-path quirk.
- **AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM** (open) — "Dev-mode write-back: gym Save to repo persists bot tuning": the same "dev writes to tracked repo data" family; keep separate.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-broad guard breaks the legit dev save flow** — mitigation: scope the refusal to (a) targets outside the active root and (b) test-mode; the dev-mode save path from the active checkout must keep working (AC2 keeps explicit-root fixtures valid).
- **Stray server on the happy-dom origin (localhost:3000) still receives writes if only the plugin changes** — the store-level test-mode guard (AC3) is the belt-and-braces fix; do not rely on the plugin alone.
- **Root-cause mechanism partially inferred** — the exact process that answers the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run was not reproduced deterministically in this intake; the implementer must reproduce and confirm before finalising the guard wording (record the reproduction in the work item). Non-blocking for the fix: ACs are observable-outcome based.
- **Scope creep** — protecting against an operator's accidental save overwriting a tuned config in the *browser/UI* (e.g. a confirmation prompt) is a separate UX concern; record it as a separate item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption** — `npm --silent test` remains the audit-accepted full suite; suite runs from implement worktrees use symlinked node_modules; vitest happy-dom default origin is `http://localhost:3000` and happy-dom resolves relative fetches against it (verified in installed `vitest`/`happy-dom` sources at intake time).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed context (title + description of AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) already contained the observed symptom, the primary hypothesis (root resolution via symlinked node_modules / vite project root), and the suggested fix directions. Research performed during intake:

- **Q (self): "Which code path is the only writer of the tracked CSVs?"** — Answer (Map): `configCsvPlugin.handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath))` in `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`; `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274). Source: code inspection of `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, `vite.config.ts` (plugin registered without options).
- **Q (self): "How does a suite-run write escape the temp-fixture pattern?"** — Answer (Map): all plugin instantiations in tests pass explicit temp roots (`configCsvPlugin.test.ts` line 100/447, `configStore.integration.test.ts` line 80) and GymPlayer tests mock the store — so the leak is not from these; the store's dev-mode save issues a relative `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (configStore.ts lines 397–405, 569–586) gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV` (true under vitest). In the happy-dom integration project, happy-dom's `Fetch` resolves the relative URL against `window.location.href` (verified in `node_modules/happy-dom/lib/fetch/Fetch.js`), whose vitest default is `http://localhost:3000` (verified in `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DC7d2Pf8.js` line 343). A real server on that origin with a root at the main checkout receives the PUT.
- **Q (self): "Why does the worktree's root resolve to the main checkout?"** — Answer (Map): worktree `node_modules` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed via `ls -la` on four live worktrees), so Vite's package-root/workspace-root detection and any module-relative path resolution can escape to the main checkout. Likely, not yet reproduced end-to-end (recorded in Risks).
- **Q (self): "Why doesn't the active checkout's csv-seed test catch the leak?"** — Answer (Map): `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` reads CSVs via `resolve(__dirname, …)`, i.e. the active checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it. Source: code inspection.
- **Q (self): "Are there existing related items?"** — Answer (Map): yes — AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL (ship-config smoke failure), AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT (enemy-config analogue), AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP / AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2 (generic suite-exit-1), AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V, AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4, AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM. Source: `wl search` during intake step 2.
- **Open question for the implementer (not a producer blocker):** reproduce the exact answering server/process on the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run and record it; the ACs are outcome-verifiable regardless.

# Intake brief — Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)

## Headline

Replace the mini-boss reward choice with a **spin-the-wheel** that always
delivers a guaranteed permanent upgrade: one bonus slot upgrades everything,
5 slots upgrade 3 picks, 10 upgrade 2, and the remaining 84 upgrade 1 — so a
mini-boss victory always makes the build meaningfully stronger.

## Problem statement

Mini-boss rewards currently offer a flat menu (upgrade any one owned item, or
unlock one locked weapon) which reads as a low-value chore rather than a
reward. The player wants a moment of anticipation that *always* pays out in
power, presented as a wheel of fortune spin over the power-ups the player has
invested in permanent slots.

## Users

- **Player (core loop):** after defeating a mini-boss, expects a celebration
  and a guaranteed, tangible power gain.
- **Demo/attract bot:** must not stall on the wheel; auto-spins after the same
  human-like delay as the hold-full choice (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F contract).

### Example user story

> As a player, when I defeat a mini-boss, I want to click a button to spin a
> wheel showing the power-ups in my permanent slots, watch it slow to a stop,
> and receive the landed upgrade(s) — so the reward feels like a gamble that
> always pays out, not a to-do list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Defeating a mini-boss opens a **wheel overlay** (the multi-option
   upgrade-or-unlock choice is gone): one wedge per **owned permanent kind**
   across the shared six-slot pool — power-up kinds **and** weapon drops —
   plus a single **bonus** wedge; play is paused exactly like the hold-full
   choice.
2. Spinning is player-initiated (click/keyboard), the wheel animation starts
   fast and eases out (building tension; the outcome must not be predictable
   until it stops), and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly
   once.
3. The spin outcome follows the **100-slot distribution**: 1 slot = bonus
   (every owned permanent kind +1 level), 5 slots = 3 upgrades, 10 slots = 2
   upgrades, 84 slots = 1 upgrade. Multi-upgrade slots pick **distinct**
   owned kinds where possible and repeat a kind only when there are fewer
   owned kinds than the slot's count (a player with one owned power-up landing
   a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
4. **Empty-owned fallback:** when the player owns no permanent kinds at a
   mini-boss defeat, the wheel is not shown and the existing hold-full-style
   three-option choice is offered instead, so a mini-boss always pays out.
5. The run-scoped weapon-unlock feature and its reward options are **removed**
   from mini-boss rewards (locked-pool option builders, `getUnlockedWeapons`
   and the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field; `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bumped
   so stale checkpoints are rejected cleanly).
6. Outcomes are drawn from the **run-seeded RNG** (no `Math.random()`), the
   distribution/resolver and the reward application live in shared modules the
   game and gyms both consume, and demo mode auto-spins after
   `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD §4.4.4,
   `docs/BALANCING.md`, checkpoint notes), including code comments.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, including unit
   tests for the slot distribution/outcome resolver and PlayScene wheel-flow
   tests replacing the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): slot distribution and reward
  application must live once in shared modules consumed by `PlayScene` and any
  gym surface; no scene-private divergence.
- **Code-first visuals:** icons come from the existing code-drawn
  `src/powerups/icons.ts` (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets (GDD §7.2).
- **Seed reproducibility:** run-seeded RNG only; deterministic tests.
- **Launcher-agnostic overlay:** a single optional selection/result callback
  (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s `onSelect`), so any launcher can drive it.
- No ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation (test-slot policy); changed
  scope is run via the test skill.

## Existing state

- Defeating a mini-boss fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` → `openMiniBossReward`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`), which offers **one** upgrade-or-unlock choice:
  every owned permanent weapon/power-up level-up offer (built by
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`) plus every still-locked weapon from
  `MINI_BOSS_LOCKED_WEAPONS` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`). The overlay is the
  shared `MineralChoiceScene`; selection applies `applyMineralChoiceReward`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`, re-exported by
  `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`). Rewards are applied exactly once
  (`selectMiniBossReward` resets the open flag). See GDD §4.4.4
  (AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH).
- **Note (stale description):** the description's "choice of 5 random power
  ups" does not match current behaviour — the live reward is the
  upgrade-or-unlock menu described above; the wheel replaces *that*.
- Each wheel-relevant decision is a permanent kind in a **shared 6-slot pool**
  (`src/powerups/slots.ts`) covering both power-up kinds and weapon drops;
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) tracks permanent vs
  temporary levels and per-kind caps; the checkpoint
  (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) persists weapon/power-up levels and
  `unlockedWeapons` (the latter is removed by AC5).
- Demo mode already auto-selects the reward via `_randomDemoRewardIndex()`
  after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) — reuse this
  seam for auto-spin.

## Desired change

- New pure module (e.g. `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`): the 100-slot
  distribution (1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single), a weighted
  outcome resolver over owned permanent kinds, distinct-kind multi-upgrade
  selection (repeats only when fewer kinds than picks), cap-aware handling,
  injectable RNG.
- New launcher-agnostic overlay (e.g. `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`): one
  wedge per owned icon plus the bonus wedge, pointer, fast-starting/eased-out
  spin, landed-wedge highlight, click/keyboard to spin, result callback.
  Register in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward`: launch the
  wheel with the owned permanent kinds (from `resolveSlotState`/
  `getWeaponLevels`/`getPowerUpLevels`), apply the resolved outcome once
  through the shared reward machinery, fall back to the three-option choice
  when nothing is owned, and keep demo auto-spin.
- Remove the unlock feature (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts` locked-pool state and
  option builders, `PlayScene.getUnlockedWeapons`, the checkpoint
  `unlockedWeapons` field) and bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- Update GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` and checkpoint docs.
- Replace the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests in
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`; add deterministic unit tests for the
  distribution and outcome resolver.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — rework `openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward` to the wheel flow; fallback; demo auto-spin; drop unlock state.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (new) — pure 100-slot distribution + weighted outcome resolver, distinct-kind picks, caps.
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new) — launcher-agnostic wheel overlay: wedges, spin + ease-out animation, pointer, result callback.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — reuse `drawPowerUpIcon`/`drawWeaponIcon` for wheel wedges.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — owned permanent kinds feeding the wheel population.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — unlock machinery to be removed (AC5).
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` / `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — shared reward application for spin outcomes.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register the wheel scene.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — remove `unlockedWeapons`; bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — exercise the shared wheel/reward path (parity).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` (new) — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool (current behaviour being replaced).
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — AI bot reward-screen selection (demo auto-select contract to preserve).
- AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF — six-slot permanent loadout accounting (slot pool the wheel reads).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — power-up level store (permanent levels/caps applied by the wheel).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (shared modules requirement).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice overlay (pattern the wheel scene mirrors).

- AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD — Mini-boss/boss strength scales with player firepower (completed; adjacent balance context for reward power).

No test command is executed. Consequences observed while implementing AH-0MVLJF886009584F:

## Problem statement

The PlayScene integration test `PlayScene — Robotron homing horde (AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6) > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) failed once during the AI_Hell full suite (heavy machine load) and passed on a fresh full-suite re-run minutes later with identical code. It is a flaky test, not a gameplay regression, and it is the last remaining kill test in this file that has not been hardened against non-deterministic scene state.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full suite** — a red full-suite gate blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage items and retries.
- **Developers of the Robotron horde (and shared kill seam)** — they need the horde kill/accounting contract to stay proven while the test stays stable.

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want the Robotron horde kill test to pass deterministically so that an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by it.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the wave-accounting contract (a horde kill counted exactly once) still asserted, so the fix does not hide a real regression.*

## Existing state (evidence)

Failure from the `implement.py finish` gate for AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H (docs-only change, cannot affect kill behaviour):

```
FAIL |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6168:26
    6166|     scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
    6167|     scene.tick(0.001);
    6168|     expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
```

Same run also printed repeated `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` on stderr (unrelated noise; no test failed on it).

The current test body (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6174-6184`) is:

```ts
const victim = liveGrunts(scene)[0];
scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
scene.tick(0.001);
expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
expect(wm.enemiesAlive).toBe(total - 1);
```

Two facts narrow the cause:

1. **The test is non-deterministic per run, independent of load.** `bootWithHordeWave()` never injects an RNG or run seed, so `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` draws a fresh `randomSeed()` (`Math.random()`, `src/core/rng.ts`) each run and the horde plan (`computeHordeSpawns`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts`) places the 16 grunts at RNG-jittered points along the four arena edges. The passing re-run therefore re-drew a different layout; "passed on re-run" is *not* evidence that load is the variable.
2. **The identical scenario has already been fixed one describe-block earlier.** `killing a pursuer advances wave accounting exactly once` (Pac-Man pursuer) had the same single-`tick(0.001)` shape and the same flake, and was fixed by wrapping the kill in the existing module-level `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` helper (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:397-410`, documented as AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK): it stubs `getEnemyEntities()` to the victim only and disables auto-fire for the duration, so "auto-fire or an overlapping pursuer cannot add a second kill and double-decrement the wave accounting". The Robotron horde kill test is the *unhardened sibling* of that test — it predates/omits the isolation.

The description's original hypothesis ("the physics/collision step for that tick may not process the new projectile before the assertion") is **not** supported: `scene.tick(dt)` is a synchronous call that runs the full player/auto-fire/bullet/collision/accounting pass in one go (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1265+`), so a longer tick cannot make a pass "complete"; what changes with a longer tick is *how much extra state* (auto-fire bullets, homing movement, wave timer) participates in that pass.

## Diagnosis to confirm during implementation

Confirm the exact mechanism before changing the assertion. Candidate mechanisms, in order of likelihood:

1. **Auto-fire / other-bullet interference** — the scene's auto-fire is live in this scenario, so a shot fired in the same tick can hit a grunt (or a different, overlapping grunt) and shift which entity the spawned bullet resolves against. The pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) fixed exactly this with `isolateEnemyForKill`.
2. **Overlapping horde grunts** — grunts in one spawn group share an edge and can be placed close enough that a bullet placed on the victim is also within an earlier-iterated grunt's hit radius.
3. **Wave-phase/`paused` gating** — a wave-timeout transition switches `tick()` to the carried-survivor-only collision pass (`_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`), and a paused scene makes `tick()` a no-op; either would leave the victim alive. Check `scene.isTransitioning()` / `paused` under the failing seed.
4. **Wall-clock frames before the loop is stopped** — `bootScene()` resumes the live RAF loop, and `advanceGame()` stops it only after a microtask yield, so real frames with real deltas run before the deterministic stepping begins (load-dependent state drift). Relevant if the failure reproduces without seed isolation.

Reproduce deterministically (seed sweep): inject a fixed seed via `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(<seed>))` before `scene.restart()` and sweep seeds until the failure reproduces, then fix and verify that seed. Prefer the narrowest fix that removes the interference.

Steps to reproduce (seed sweep):

1. In `bootWithHordeWave()`, add `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` before `scene.scene.restart()` (import `createSeededRng` from `../core/rng`).
2. Loop seeds (e.g. `0..999`) in a temporary harness or repeated test-skill runs until `victim.alive` is `true` after the kill step; note the seed.
3. Record the seed and the observed mechanism on this work item, then apply the fix and re-verify that seed plus a broader sweep.

## Desired change

Make the horde kill test deterministic **without weakening what it proves**:

- Isolate the kill exactly as the pursuer test does — reuse `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` (`auto-fire` off, only the victim visible to the collision pass) — and/or pin the scene RNG to a fixed seed so the horde layout is reproducible.
- Keep the single-tick kill if it is deterministic after isolation; otherwise use a small bounded "tick until the victim dies" loop (guard counter, e.g. ≤ 20 frames of `0.016`) and assert the *outcome*.
- Still assert that the victim dies **and** that wave accounting drops by exactly one — and, to prove "exactly once", assert the accounting is unchanged after further ticks (no double decrement).

## Acceptance criteria

- The flaky failure is reproduced deterministically first (fixed seed and/or a temporary repeat-run harness), and the observed mechanism is recorded as a comment on this work item with the failing seed (or an explicit statement that no seed reproduces it, with the evidence gathered).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` passes on repeated runs: at least 20 consecutive runs of `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` via the test skill, and at least one run with an additional concurrent load-generating job active, all green.
- The test still proves the contract: the victim grunt is dead after the kill step, and `wm.enemiesAlive` is exactly `total - 1` (and stays `total - 1` after further ticks — a kill is never counted twice). The "exactly once" proof is not weakened to "at most once".
- The fix is confined to test code (plus test comments); no gameplay behaviour, RNG semantics, or `isSpawning`/collision logic changes. If investigation shows a genuine gameplay defect is being masked, stop and record it as a new work item (`discovered-from:AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU`) rather than loosening the test.
- If the fix pattern is reusable (e.g. other horde/pursuer kill tests), note it in the test comment referencing AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU and AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK so the next reader sees why the isolation is required.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`) — no ad-hoc `vitest`/`npm test`. Repeated-run verification is therefore a test-skill invocation with a narrow scope (changed-scope gate) plus the full-suite gate at push.
- **No assertion weakening:** a longer tick alone is acceptable only if it is deterministic after isolation; it must not become a "sleep until it works" loop with an unbounded guard.
- **No production-code behaviour change:** the horde kill path (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`) is shared with every gym (`src/scenes/core/`), so a behavioural change would require gym-parity work — out of scope unless a real defect is found.
- Prefer reusing existing helpers (`isolateEnemyForKill`, `finishSpawnSequence`) over introducing a new pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — horde kill test at ~6174; `bootWithHordeWave`/`releaseHorde` helpers at ~6089-6124; existing `isolateEnemyForKill` helper at ~397-410 to reuse.
- `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` — RNG-driven spawn placement (`computeHordeSpawns`) explaining per-run layout variance.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `planHordeSpawns` / `_releaseDueHordeSpawns` (~2164-2245), `tick` collision/phase ordering (~1265-1390), `_initRunSeed` (~4849-4863).
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()` (`Math.random`-seeded runs by default).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene`/`advanceGame` deterministic harness (frame-loop stop/resume behaviour).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies` (~1189) and `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` (~384) — read-only context for the interference analysis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no gameplay defect is being masked. If the isolated test still fails for a fixed seed, the flake may reflect a real horde/accounting bug — escalate as a new (child) work item instead of widening the tick.
- **Risk:** adding `scene.setRng(...)` in this describe block changes the RNG stream for the other four horde tests in the same block; keep the seed pinned in a `beforeEach`-style helper or per-test so assertions like "spawns the configured horde" stay valid.
- **Risk:** a bounded tick loop can hide a regression that makes kills take longer; keep the bound small (≈ 0.32 s simulated) and assert exactly-once accounting afterwards.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other single-tick kill tests in the same file (asteroids, boss phases) use `tick(0.016)` and have not flaked; do not refactor them wholesale — record as separate work if desired.
- **Risk:** flake attribution — a green re-run under load is weak evidence; the fix must be justified by a *reproduced deterministic* failure, not by "it passed 20 times".
- **Risk:** `isolateEnemyForKill` stubs `getEnemyEntities` and `autoFireEnabled` on the instance and must be restored in a `finally` block (as the pursuer test does); a leaked stub would silently affect later tests in the same file.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK** (completed) — `[test-failure] PlayScene — flaky wave-accounting kill tests (Harvester + Pac-Man pursuer)`; introduced `isolateEnemyForKill` for exactly this interference class. Direct precedent.
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** (completed) — `Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load`; load-sensitivity remediation (deterministic boot/frames).
- **AH-0MV5JRAH90034PKR** (completed) — `Flaky Centipede chain bounds assertion under full-suite load`; fixed "advanced 20 s in one tick" by stepping in 0.05 s increments — precedent for tick-size fixes in this file.
- **AH-0MVFPMT4P005UHZL** — removed the last wall-clock waits from the suites (`advanceGame` / `stepGameUntil`); the deterministic harness this test relies on.
- **AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6** — the Robotron homing horde feature these tests cover.
- **AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H** (completed) — docs-only change whose gate surfaced this flake (`discovered-from`).
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — repo guard documenting the flake history and the supported deterministic replacements.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent consideration):** "Is the failure load-induced (wall-clock frame drift) or seed-induced (random horde layout)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence, no producer input needed):** seed-induced is demonstrable from the code — `bootWithHordeWave` injects no RNG, so `_initRunSeed()` draws `randomSeed()` per run and `computeHordeSpawns` places grunts at RNG-jittered edge positions. The pass-on-re-run therefore used a different layout. Load may additionally drift scene state via live RAF frames before `advanceGame` stops the loop, but that is not required to explain the flake. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4849-4863`, `src/core/rng.ts:49`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` (`computeHordeSpawns`).
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Does the description's proposed fix (`scene.tick(0.05)` / tick-until-dead) actually address the mechanism?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** only partially. `scene.tick(dt)` is synchronous, so "the collision step did not process the projectile" cannot happen; the pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) shows the real interference was auto-fire / overlapping entities, fixed by `isolateEnemyForKill`. The brief therefore requires isolation (plus a fixed seed) as the primary fix, with a bounded tick loop only as a secondary robustness measure.
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Should the fix change gameplay code (e.g. horde collision ordering)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo constraints):** no. Any gameplay change is shared with every gym and would require gym-parity work; a genuine defect would be filed as a new work item instead. Assumption recorded in *Risks & assumptions*.
- **Producer input:** none required — the item's goal and acceptance criteria are unambiguous and the remaining decisions are resolved by repo evidence and precedent. Recorded here for auditability; no open questions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUJRVYWG006NJUU** – Shared multi-hit kill finalisation (completed) — the shared kill seam this test's bullet path runs through.
- **AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS** – Shared mineral kill-drop helper + PlayScene/BaseEnemy refactor (completed) — touches the same enemy-kill finalisation path.

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — gym↔game parity convention (§5.1), relevant to the "no behaviour change" constraint.
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — documents this flake family and the supported deterministic replacements.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `isolateEnemyForKill` helper (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) reused by the fix.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

## Goal (vertical slice)

Extend the proven music path with the Phrygian Dominant combat layer — Combat Motifs A and B and the combat progression — that transitions in from the ambient state at a bar boundary, stays locked to the shared beat grid, ducks under key SFX, and is driven by PlayScene and the gym scenes identically (gym-game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Wave start transitions menu/ambient -> combat at a bar boundary, and Combat Motif A ("Incoming Wave") introduces the combat state.
- [ ] Combat music tempo is coherent with the game beatBpm (locked to it, or documented as intentionally independent), and never fights the player-fire grid.
- [ ] Ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified: music ducks under key SFX cues so SFX intelligibility is preserved, and this is covered by tests.

# Shard Swarm — fire/impact VFX & SFX

**discovered-from:AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW** (5 net-new weapon types) — audit of the `shard_swarm` player weapon found it shipped with an in-flight bullet look only: no fire sound, no muzzle flash and no per-weapon impact feedback.

## Current state (audit evidence)

Present:
- In-flight identity: `bulletShape: 'shard'` + overrides (`bulletShapeLength: 1.6`, `bulletTrail: 1.2`, `bulletSize: 0.72`, lime `BULLET_COLORS.shard_swarm = 0xc0ff33`) in `src/utils/weapons.ts:1336`, rendered through the shared bullet-shape seam (`_shard` in `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`).
- Code-drawn lime fan icon (`drawShardSwarmIcon`, `src/powerups/icons.ts:1121`).

Missing:
- **No fire SFX.** `playWeaponFireSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:628`) has no `shard_swarm` case, so it falls through to the `default:` no-op — the weapon fires silently in live play, in the hold-full metronome and in every gym.
- **No muzzle flash.** The definition declares no `muzzleFlash` metadata, and `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:896`) only spawns the launch cue `if (def.muzzleFlash)`.
- **No per-weapon impact feedback.** No `impactFx` spec, so `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()` returns early: no baked hit cue (the impact is silent) and only the generic warm-white flash (`spawnBulletImpact`, `0xfff2a0`, r7, `CombatScene.ts:434`) rather than a lime shard-coloured one. The fan therefore reads as weak noise against the neon background at 0.72× bullet scale.

## Goal (user story)

As a player holding the Shard Swarm, I want an audible launch and hit so I can hear that the five-shard fan is firing and connecting, and I want the shards and their impacts to punch clearly against the neon field, so the weapon feels as distinctive in the hand as its silhouette suggests — without any change to its balance.

## Scope

`shard_swarm` only. Feel/visual/audio only — no behaviour or balance change: fire rate (750 ms, once per beat), the five offsets (±15°, ±7.5°, 0°), bullet lifetime (0.55 s → ~193 px reach), speed, size and colour stay exactly as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Audible fire.** `playWeaponFireSound('shard_swarm')` routes to a new baked ToneForge fire cue (recipe `aihell-shard-swarm-fire`, rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`), so live fire, the hold-full metronome and gym fire all sound identical through the one shared path (`src/audio/effects.ts`, `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`-adjacent registry pattern).
- **Audible, visibly distinct impact.** `shard_swarm` declares an `impactFx` spec (`color` = lime-family, `radius`, `duration`, `cue`) resolved through `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()`, producing a lime-tinted impact flash and a new baked hit cue (`aihell-shard-swarm-impact`) so the game and every gym connect identically. The generic white fallback flash no longer applies to this weapon.
- **Muzzle flash + more noticeable in-flight VFX.** The definition declares `muzzleFlash` metadata (lime, sized for a five-shard burst) spawned through the shared `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `spawnMuzzleFlash` path, and the shards are made more legible in flight (e.g. slightly stronger rim/spine contrast and/or a brighter trail) through the shared `bulletVisuals` seam — no per-scene copies, no new bespoke rendering path.
- **Gym↔game parity.** All changes land in the shared core/seams (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`, `src/vfx/`, `src/audio/`) and are consumed identically by `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; `CombatScene.equivalence` and the gym-parity/documentation roster guards pass unchanged.
- **Docs + audio catalogue updated.** `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` records both new cues with their recipes and seeds, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` lists them, and the per-weapon visual roster guards (`src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisualRoster.test.ts`) plus README/GDD §4.4/§7.3 per-weapon notes include the Shard Swarm's fire and impact identity instead of listing it as visual-only.
- **No new legibility regressions.** The five-shard fan at full upgrade levels (extra projectiles, larger bullets) must not become a screen-filling blur: the impact/muzzle flashes are rate-limited by the natural 750 ms cadence and the effect sizes stay within the existing per-weapon effect budget.
- **Full test suite passes**, including new/updated tests for the fire cue dispatch, `impactFx` resolution, muzzle-flash spawn, and the audio cue contract test (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`).

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `shard_swarm` `muzzleFlash` / `impactFx` metadata
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — ensure the new metadata survives level resolution
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` — in-flight `shard` legibility for the player weapon
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playWeaponFireSound` case + impact cue registry + `playShardSwarm*Sound` exports
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-shard-swarm-{fire,impact}.yaml`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact seams (consume-only; no new hook needed if the metadata path suffices)
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README, GDD §4.4 / §7.3

## Known sibling gap (not in this item's scope)

The same missing feel package (`muzzleFlash`, `impactFx`, fire cue) applies to the other four net-new unlock-pool weapons from AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW: `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `heavy_slug`. Railgun SFX is already tracked by Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA); the remaining three have no item yet. The metadata/pipeline work here should be structured so those can reuse it unchanged.

## Risks / notes

- ToneForge assets are baked, not runtime-synthesised (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` is the sole runtime exception): new cues need recipe YAML + a `scripts/build-audio.sh` run, and the seeds must be recorded.
- Audio must remain a safe no-op in headless tests (no audio context).

# We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)

## Objective

**User story (producer).** As the producer, I want the region/home-world proposal
plus **two genuinely different** outer-loop candidates, each written up as a
decision-ready outline on the same footing, so that I can choose one and have it
written into the Game Design Document (GDD) with confidence.

**User story (player).** As a player, I want something to carry forward between
runs — a long-term goal and a sense that my play changes the world — so that
losing a run does not mean losing all progress, and so that beating the final
boss is a milestone on the way to winning rather than the end of everything.

## Users

- **Producer / designer (primary).** Chooses one of three outlined loops and owns
  the GDD write-up; needs comparable, honest outlines and a defensible ranking.
- **Player (arcade / bullet-hell fan).** Needs a reason to return after a lost
  run and a goal beyond a high score; wants progress that survives failure.
- **Developer / agent implementing the loop later.** Needs each outline to name
  the systems, seams and gym coverage so the chosen loop can be planned without
  re-deriving the design.

## Problem statement

The game has a strong **inner loop** (flying, dodging formations, destroying
enemies) and a functioning **middle loop** (per-run ship upgrading through
minerals → hold-full power-up choices → levelled weapons), but **no outer loop**:
nothing persists between runs except a leaderboard score, player settings and a
single run checkpoint. A death ends the run outright (GDD §4.6: "There is no
continue mechanic. Game over is final"), so long-term engagement rests entirely
on score chasing. The fiction ("pilot a resistance ship through a digital
underworld ruled by rogue AI") implies a war to be won, but the game currently
has no structure that represents winning it.

The producer has proposed one candidate outer loop (contested regions with a
home world to find and defend) and asked for **two other candidates** to be
brainstormed and outlined, after which the producer chooses one for the GDD.

## Deliverable

A single design-exploration document — `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — built
to the same standard as the existing research catalogues
(`docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`):
selected candidates written up per-concept, a "considered but not selected"
section, and a selection recommendation. It is a **design document only**: no
gameplay code, no persistence schema changes and no new scenes are implemented
in this item.

The producer's choice is then written into the GDD as a follow-on work item; this
item ends at the candidate document, the comparison and the recommendation.

## Loop tiers used by the document

| Tier | Timescale | Definition in this game | Exists today? |
|------|-----------|-------------------------|---------------|
| **Inner** | Seconds | Flying, dodging, destroying enemies and formations within a wave | Yes (GDD §2.3–2.6) |
| **Middle** | Minutes (a run) | Ship upgrading: minerals → hold-full power-up/weapon choices, levelled effects, extra lives | Yes (GDD §4.4, §4.6) |
| **Outer** | Hours (a campaign / a season) | What the player carries **between** runs and what they are ultimately trying to achieve | **No** |

## Candidate A — Contested Regions / Home World (producer's proposal)

Recorded as proposed, not redesigned. Its outline must preserve every named
mechanic:

- Space is divided into **regions**; each region has an **AI aggression level**.
- The ship can **warp a limited distance** to adjacent regions.
- The goal is to find a region with **zero aggression** containing a **planet
  that can become home to the humans**.
- Having found it, the player must **defend all adjacent regions** against
  attack by aggressive AI.
- The player may leave their **fully upgraded ship** in a region with an **AI
  automated pilot** that defends that region.
- The player then returns home and **collects another ship with no upgrades**,
  and must go out again to make it strong enough to be left guarding another
  region.
- **Factional AI warfare** changes region strength over time: warring AI
  factions fight over a region and the winner leaves a stronger force there.
- **Win condition:** all regions have successfully defended against a massive AI
  onslaught, at which point the home world is safe and the game is won.

The outline must state its **minimal first slice** (the smallest version that
proves the loop is fun), because the full proposal is the largest of the three.

## Candidate B — Salvage Fleet (proposed direction, resource-persistent meta)

A **roguelite meta-progression** outer loop that leaves the map alone and
persists **player power** instead.

- Between runs the player spends **banked salvage** (minerals and mini-boss AI
  cores extracted at the existing checkpoint moments) in a persistent **hangar**
  to unlock hulls, starting weapons and permanent modifiers.
- Each run is a **deployment** flown in one chosen hull; losing the run forfeits
  that run's unbanked salvage but never the hangar.
- The outer goal is to assemble a fleet strong enough for a final assault run at
  maximum threat.
- Progression axis: **build/economy** (what the player owns), not territory.

## Candidate C — Signal Decode (proposed direction, knowledge-persistent meta)

A **campaign-mutating** outer loop where the thing that persists is
**information**.

- Mini-bosses and the boss drop **data fragments** that assemble a persistent
  codex revealing the origin of the AI and the "hellscape" it generates.
- Codex knowledge **mutates and unlocks the campaign** (new enemy behaviours,
  hellscape modifiers, shortcuts), and the final confrontation only becomes
  winnable once the core's rules have been decoded — the boss's phases are the
  codex's payoff.
- Progression axis: **knowledge and campaign variation**, not territory or
  currency.

## Required outline structure (every candidate)

1. **Fantasy / pitch** — one paragraph, in the game's fiction.
2. **Loop structure** — moment-to-moment → run → meta, with an explicit
   statement of *what carries between runs*.
3. **States** — win, lose, partial progress and what a bad run still advances.
4. **New systems** required (named, with rough size).
5. **Reuse of existing systems** — checkpoint (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`),
   minerals/power-up levels, `Leaderboard`, difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`), mini-boss rewards, bot/attract mode.
6. **Persistence and save model** — a sketch `localStorage` payload under
   §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend) with migration note.
7. **Session shape** — target run length and hours-to-win.
8. **UI / scene surface** — which new screens or menu entries are needed.
9. **Gym testability and the bot** — how its gameplay additions can be exercised
   in a gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule) and how attract mode can complete
   or avoid stalling on the outer loop.
10. **Pillar impact** — which current GDD pillars it changes (e.g. "no continue,
    game over is final", the single final boss), stated explicitly.
11. **Effort and risk** — sized honestly, with the failure modes that would make
    the loop unfun.
12. **Minimal first slice** — the smallest shippable version.

A **comparison table** then ranks all candidates on: fit with the existing
pilots-in-a-digital-hell fiction, reuse of shipped systems, new-system cost,
persistence complexity, session length fit, legibility of progress to the player,
gym/bot testability, and risk of trivialising or gutting the shipped campaign —
followed by an explicit **recommendation with rationale** and why the others rank
lower. A "Considered but not selected" section records further ideas (e.g. an
arcade-style tiered mutator ladder, a pure daily-seed challenge ladder) with a
one-line deferral reason each.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deliverable exists and frames the problem.** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   exists, opens with the inner/middle/outer tier definitions above and the
   comparison criteria, and states that it is design-only.
2. **Candidate A is complete and faithful.** Candidate A is written up with all
   twelve required sections and preserves every mechanic listed in *Candidate A*
   above (regions, limited warp, per-region aggression, zero-aggression home
   region with a habitable planet, defence of adjacent regions, autonomous-pilot
   ship hand-off, unupgraded replacement ship, faction warfare, all-regions-held
   win). No proposed mechanic is silently dropped, altered or merged.
3. **Two additional candidates, materially distinct.** Candidates B and C each
   carry all twelve required sections and each names *what persists between
   runs* differently from Candidate A and from each other; each is justified
   against at least one named design pillar or fiction element.
4. **Decision-ready comparison.** The document contains a comparison table across
   the agreed criteria, an explicit recommendation with rationale, and a ranked
   justification for why the two non-recommended candidates rank lower.
5. **Alternatives recorded.** A "Considered but not selected" section lists at
   least two further outer-loop ideas with a one-line deferral reason each.
6. **Docs guard test.** A vitest docs-guard test (convention:
   `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`) asserts the document exists,
   contains the tier definitions, the comparison table and, for each of the three
   candidates, the twelve required section headings — so the deliverable cannot
   silently regress. It passes in the changed-scope test gate.
7. **Cross-linked, not orphaned.** The new document is cross-linked from the GDD
   future-scope section (§8) and from where the other design catalogues are
   referenced in `README.md`; every added link resolves to a file or anchor that
   exists.
8. **Producer decision is staged, not pre-empted.** The document ends with a
   "Producer decision record" section (candidate | decision | date | notes) left
   pending, plus a note that the chosen loop's GDD write-up is a follow-on work
   item. No GDD gameplay text for the chosen loop is written in this item.
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `README.md`, and the GDD cross-links.
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Design only.** No gameplay, persistence-schema or scene implementation in
  this item; each candidate is marked "design only, not scheduled".
- **No backend.** All persistence must fit the existing `localStorage` model
  (GDD §6.6) with defensive parsing, as the leaderboard and checkpoint do.
- **Engine policy.** Candidates must not require a new engine or editor-driven
  content (GDD §6.1: code-first, Phaser).
- **Pillars are explicit, not accidental.** A candidate may propose changing an
  existing pillar (e.g. "no continue", the single final boss) but must say so in
  its *Pillar impact* section with a rationale and a cost.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any gameplay element a candidate proposes must be
  exercisable in a gym scene, and the outline must say how (AGENTS.md parity
  rule, `src/scenes/gym/`, `GymFormationScene`).
- **Attract mode must not stall.** The demo bot must be able to traverse or skip
  any new outer-loop UI (§2.1 attract/demo mode).
- **Scope discipline.** Opportunities discovered mid-draft become linked work
  items, not added scope.
- **Write location and language.** Deliverable lives in `docs/` (no planning
  documents in the repo root); UK English and Markdown throughout.
- **Session shape must be stated.** Each candidate names its target run length
  and its hours-to-win, so the producer can compare commitment.

## Existing state

- **Inner/middle loops shipped:** 10-level campaign, 100 waves, 10 mini-bosses,
  one multi-phase final boss (GDD §3, §4.6); minerals and hold-full power-up
  choices are the middle loop's currency (§4.4); difficulty scaling is data-driven
  (`src/core/levelScaling.ts`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`).
- **Persistence today:** `ai_hell_leaderboard` (top-10 scores), `ai_hell_settings`,
  `ai_hell_checkpoint` (auto-written at each mini-boss defeat and offering
  "Continue — Level N"), `ai_hell_lastSession` (GDD §6.6).
- **No meta layer:** no persistent currency, unlock tree, map/region structure or
  cross-run progression of any kind. Game over is final (GDD §4.6).
- **Design-document precedent:** `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` and
  `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` are the established pattern for
  candidate-selection research, each with a sibling docs-guard test
  (`src/classicEnemyResearchDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`).

## Desired change

The repo gains one decision-ready design document describing three outer-loop
candidates on equal footing, with a comparison, a recommendation, deferral
reasons for rejected ideas and a docs guard that keeps the document honest — so
the producer can choose one loop with full information and the GDD write-up can
start immediately afterwards.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — **new**; the deliverable (candidate outlines,
  comparison, recommendation, deferrals, producer decision record).
- `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` — **new**; docs guard asserting the
  document's required sections and per-candidate headings, following the
  `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts` convention.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **edit**; §8 Future Scope cross-link to the new
  document (no gameplay text for a candidate in this item).
- `README.md` — **edit**; add the new document where the other design catalogues
  are referenced.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — **reference only**; the existing between-level
  persistence seam any outer loop will build on.
- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` —
  **reference only**, to ground each candidate's reuse claims.

## Out of scope

- Implementing any candidate's systems (map, currency, codex, hangar, regions).
- Writing the chosen loop into the GDD as playable specification (follow-on item).
- Balancing or tuning anything that already ships.
- CHANGELOG.md (managed by the release pipeline).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — deliverable shape.** "Brainstorm two other possible outer loops
  and write an outline for each" is read as a design-exploration deliverable in
  `docs/`, matching the existing research-catalogue precedent, with Candidate A
  (the producer's proposal) included so the two alternatives are compared fairly.
- **Assumption — no implementation.** "I will choose one to be written up in the
  GDD" means the GDD write-up is the *next* item, so this item stops at the
  decision-ready document.
- **Risk — pillar conflict.** Every attractive outer loop tends to break "game
  over is final" or the single-final-boss structure; mitigated by the mandatory
  *Pillar impact* section and by stating each candidate's cost explicitly.
- **Risk — Candidate A is very large** (region graph, autonomous pilots, faction
  simulation). Mitigated by requiring a *Minimal first slice* per candidate.
- **Risk — scope creep into implementation** while drafting. Mitigated by the
  design-only constraint and by filing discovered opportunities as linked work
  items.
- **Risk — over-specified docs guard.** The guard asserts headings and required
  terms only, never prose wording, so the document stays editable.
- **Risk — comparison feels arbitrary.** Mitigated by publishing the criteria in
  the document before the candidates (AC1) and ranking against each.

## Related work

- **Game Design Document for AI_Hell (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — the living GDD this
  document feeds; §2.3–2.6 (inner loop), §4.4/§4.6 (middle loop, level
  progression), §5–§6 (leaderboard, save data), §8 (future scope).
- **Checkpoint save/resume (AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51)** — the existing persistence
  precedent the outer loop extends or replaces.
- **New enemies from classic arcade games (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52)** and
  **New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4)** —
  the candidate-selection research pattern this document follows.
- **Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry
  (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4)** — the bot that must remain able to traverse any new
  outer-loop UI without stalling.
- **Update campaign documentation for 10-level structure (AH-0MV39AQOY006I083)** —
  the campaign-structure documentation the outer loop will eventually supersede
  as the game's framing.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience
  (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775)** — the validation lens the recommendation must survive.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No interactive interview round was run in this pass: the item was auto-dispatched
by the herdr downtime worker (comment `AH-C0MVNVFKO4004PPDH`) and no
ask-further-questions permission was recorded, so the requirements were clarified
from the item text, the GDD and the repo per the intake workflow's
no-questions path. The questions below are recorded with the assumption actually
adopted, so the producer can correct any of them without re-running intake.

- **Q1: Is the deliverable a design document, or does the item also expect the
  outer loop to be built?**
  — Adopted answer: **design document only.** Evidence: the item text ends "write
  an outline for each. I will choose one to be written up in the GDD", which
  places implementation and GDD specification after the producer's choice.
  Source: work-item description. Status: assumptive, correctable.
  **Recommended (had it been asked):** design-only — it matches the producer's
  stated sequence and keeps the item completable.

- **Q2: Where should the brainstorm live, and should it include the producer's
  own region proposal?**
  — Adopted answer: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, following the
  `docs/CLASSIC_*_RESEARCH.md` catalogue precedent, **including** the producer's
  proposal as Candidate A so the two alternatives are compared on equal footing.
  Evidence: GDD and README already reference the research catalogues; the item's
  proposal is recorded verbatim in the work item. Source: repo survey.
  **Recommended:** include Candidate A — comparing two alternatives against no
  baseline would make the recommendation untrustworthy.

- **Q3: Which two additional candidate directions should be explored?**
  — Adopted answer: **resource-persistent** (Salvage Fleet roguelite meta) and
  **knowledge-persistent** (Signal Decode campaign-mutating), because they differ
  from Candidate A's territorial axis in the thing that carries between runs
  (power/economy and information respectively), which makes the comparison
  meaningful rather than three re-skins of one idea. Evidence: Candidate A's axis
  is space/territory; nothing in the repo fixes an alternative. Source: repo and
  GDD survey. Status: assumptive, correctable — the producer may substitute
  directions.
  **Recommended:** these two — they span the three archetypal outer loops
  (territory, power, knowledge) that arcade-scale games actually use.

# Unit tests: player Phase Shift unmistakable layers

Test-first contract for the player path of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU (approach C,
aggressive activation edge / soft sustained state). Write these as failing
tests first; the implementation children make them pass.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the *unmistakable* player treatment pinned by tests
before it is built, so the layers, magnitudes, toggles and teardown cannot
regress and the no-shake guarantee cannot be silently dropped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pure params model.** `resolvePhaseShiftJuiceParams()` maps every new tunable
  and `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle verbatim (flash, vignette, distortion burst,
  sustained filter, widened split), with no Phaser import in the pure path.
- **Activation edge (aggressive).** A single `update(true, dt)` rising edge
  creates the full activation layer set — dim + split + surge pair + full-screen
  flash + vignette + the camera-filter distortion burst — exactly once, and a
  second `update(true, dt)` in the same phase does not duplicate any layer.
- **Sustained state (soft).** While active, deterministic `dt` ticks drive the
  split oscillation/flicker/colour-pulse and the sustained filter layer without
  allocating new game objects per frame (asserted by object-count stability
  across N ticks).
- **Exact teardown.** On the falling edge every overlay is destroyed, every
  camera filter added by the treatment is removed from the camera filter list,
  the registry is emptied, and a re-activation cycle produces a fresh, single
  layer set (no leak, no duplicate).
- **Renderer fallback.** With the renderer reporting non-WebGL (or a camera with
  no `filters`), the treatment applies the overlay layers only, never throws and
  never touches a filter API; the same suite passes headless.
- **No camera shake.** The retained regression test still asserts the treatment
  never calls `camera.shake` in any phase of the cycle.
- **Test style.** Deterministic (`dt` ticks, no sleeps/randomness), using the
  shared `VfxStubScene` / `bootScene` harness.
- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge. (verified by this item's tests)
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer. (verified by this item's tests)
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing. (verified by this item's tests)
- Distinctness and parity preserved: visually distinct from player-death juice, never shakes the camera, gym-game parity guards green, headless no-op safe. (verified by this item's tests)

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` — extend.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.test.ts` — new (probe/apply/clear contract, shared with the enemy path if reused).

## Notes

Tests must not require a real WebGL context: stub the camera filter list with a
minimal fake exposing `internal`/`external` `add*` factories, `list`, `remove`,
`clear`.

# Unit tests: unmistakable enemy emergence + wormhole ring

Test-first contract for the per-entity and wormhole parts of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU
(approach C: no screen-space effects on the emergence path).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the unmistakable emergence treatment and the wormhole
ring/shockwave pinned by tests before implementation, so the per-entity
lifecycle (create -> shimmer -> release) and the ring lifecycle cannot regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Per-enemy outline/silhouette.** `updateEnemyShimmer` creates exactly one
  outline/silhouette layer per emerging entity on its first shimmering frame,
  pulses it during the growth window, and destroys it when growth ends.
- **Widened flicker + burst.** The alpha flicker range and the leading-edge
  ripple burst magnitudes are driven verbatim from exported tunables; the burst
  decays to zero within its documented window.
- **No residual state.** After growth ends the entity's alpha, scale and blend
  mode are restored to their pre-shimmer values, the outline is gone, and the
  per-entity shimmer clock is dropped; an entity that never shimmered is
  untouched.
- **No compounding.** Running the helper twice per frame (or with variable `dt`)
  leaves the growth scale correct (absolute-value write, no drift).
- **Wormhole ring + shockwave.** `spawnWormholeOpen` creates one ring (and one
  open shockwave pulse) per wormhole, registers them in the caller's
  `wormholeEffects` registry, and `spawnWormholeClose` stops their tweens and
  destroys them exactly once (a second close or a `SHUTDOWN` does not
  double-remove).
- **Headless no-op.** All helpers construct/update with a stubbed scene (no
  `add`/`tweens`) without throwing.
- **Test style.** Deterministic scene-tick steps (`scene.tick(dt)`), no sleeps.
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer. (verified by this item's tests)
- Per-enemy emergence is unmistakable per entity: outline silhouette, stronger ripple burst, widened alpha flicker, fully restored when growth ends, no screen-wide overlay. (verified by this item's tests)
- Wormhole read: a brighter larger pulsing ring plus a one-shot open shockwave, tracked in wormholeEffects and fully cleared when the wormhole closes. (verified by this item's tests)

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — extend.

# Camera filter driver with WebGL capability probe

Shared infrastructure for approach C of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: Phaser 4 camera
filters are **WebGL only**, so every filter-based layer needs one guarded,
teardown-exact entry point.

## Goal

As a developer, I want a single shared module that can apply and clear the
Phase Shift camera-filter layers safely on any renderer, so the game and the
gyms never diverge and a headless/canvas build can never crash or leak.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Capability probe.** `supportsCameraFilters(scene)` returns true only when
  the renderer is WebGL *and* the camera exposes a usable filter list; it never
  throws for a stub, a missing camera, or a renderer without `type`.
- **Activation burst.** `applyPhaseDistortionBurst(...)` adds the pixelate +
  barrel/displacement wobble controllers for the documented duration, driven by
  the exported tunables (no hard-coded numbers).
- **Sustained layer.** `applyPhaseSustainedFilter(...)` adds the gentle
  sustained layer (low-strength glow/bloom or barrel) and returns handles for
  teardown.
- **Exact teardown.** `clearPhaseFilters(...)` removes and destroys only the
  controllers this module added, restoring the camera's pre-existing filter
  list unchanged (verified by a test that pre-adds an unrelated filter and
  asserts it survives).
- **Degradation.** When filters are unsupported every function is a documented
  no-op returning a falsy/"unsupported" result; nothing is allocated.
- **No per-frame allocation.** Steady-state updates mutate existing controller
  properties only.
- **Documented.** Module-level JSDoc explains WebGL-only behaviour, the fallback
  contract and every tunable.
- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge. (enforced by the shared driver)
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing. (enforced by the shared driver)

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.ts` — new.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.test.ts` — new (see sibling test item).

# Player Phase Shift unmistakable treatment

Implementation of the player path for AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: aggressive on the
activation edge, soft while sustained, never shaking the camera.

## Goal

As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I want the activation to read
as an unmistakable system event — a flash, a distortion hit and a strong
chromatic surge — then settle into a clearly-visible sustained shimmer, so I can
trust the state and time my flying.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Activation edge (aggressive).** The rising edge fires, in the same frame:
  a widened/stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair, a full-screen flash in a
  phase-shift palette (not the death-flash palette), a cyan edge/vignette band
  layer, and the camera distortion burst from `cameraFilters.ts`.
- **Sustained state (soft).** While phased: the vivid pulsing chromatic split
  (raised alpha and offset with the slow oscillation), the edge/vignette bands
  and the gentle sustained camera filter, all pulsing rather than static;
  sustained flicker stays at or below the documented seizure-safety cap.
- **Exact teardown.** Falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera
  filter; nothing is left on screen or in the camera filter list.
- **Toggles and tunables.** Each new layer has a `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle
  and every magnitude is an exported constant; disabling a layer leaves the rest
  working.
- **No shake.** `camera.shake` is never called (regression test retained).
- **Headless safe.** Without a render context the controller still constructs
  and updates as a no-op.
- **Tests.** The sibling test contract item passes.
- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge. (implemented here)
- Player sustained state stays continuously obvious but soft: pulsing vivid split, cyan edge vignette bands, gentle sustained camera filter, no camera shake. (implemented here)
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer. (implemented here)

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — tunables, `_apply`/`_pulseShimmer`/`_clear`.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.ts` — consumed for the filter layers.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared driver (unchanged call shape).

Discovered during intake of AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14 (discovered-from:AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14).

Follow-up from the producer's Q1 decision (a spent force-field bubble dims rather than vanishing): a permanent (hold-full) Force Field currently never regenerates its reflect budget (_forceFieldRemaining), so after the base 3 reflections it is dim (per the new spent-dim visual) and purely decorative for the rest of the run.

User story: As a player, I want a permanent Force Field to keep earning reflections over time (cf. the Thorn Field recharge, AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T), so the hold-full reward stays useful.

Acceptance criteria:
- A permanent Force Field regenerates reflections over time (interval resolved from level, cf. thorns recharge) up to its resolved budget.
- Regeneration drives the bubble from the spent-dim state back to the active look (visual follow-through from AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14).

# In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget

Discovered during **AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES** (verify fix with full suite and a
manual long-run soak), discovered-from **AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE**.

## Observation

A 5-clip full-run soak (`--count 5 --max-duration 1800000 --diagnostics`,
output written to `/tmp/ah-soak/`) completed every clip, but the process node
RSS peaked at **661.0 MiB** (clip 4 start) — above the documented **< 512 MiB**
target. The peak is not recording growth: it is `peakRssBytes` at the *start*
of a clip, carried over from the **previous** clip's end-of-clip probe, and
every clip's end-of-recording RSS was 320–388 MiB.

Cause: clips 3 (34.9 MiB) and 5 (62.75 MiB) are above the 32 MiB in-page probe
threshold, but their files sat outside the served repository root
(`/tmp/ah-soak/…`), so the probe fell back to the **in-page Blob** path
(documented fallback, reported by `probeSourceReason`). That fallback decodes
up to the 32 MiB retained prefix with `decodeAudioData` in one shot, which
inflates node RSS by a few hundred MiB temporarily. A control run of the same
workload with the output inside the repo root (`capture-output/soak/`,
600 s, 48.43 MiB) used the **streamed** probe and peaked at only **408.9 MiB**.

## Why it matters

The < 512 MiB budget is documented for a full-cap run, and `--output /tmp/…`
is a supported, documented invocation. The *path*-based fallback (and its RSS
cost) is not covered by the parent's stated fallback rationale, which only
sanctions the in-page decode for clips *below* a size threshold.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Document, in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` §Long-run memory budget, that
   the streamed probe needs the output inside the served repository root and
   that the in-page fallback costs a temporary whole-prefix audio decode
   (with the measured 661 MiB batch peak vs 408.9 MiB streamed as the
   evidence), or
2. Make the streamed probe work for outputs outside the served root (e.g. a
   temporary route serving the partial file), restoring the < 512 MiB budget
   for every supported output path.
3. Re-run a > 32 MiB clip with `--output /tmp/…` and record the peak RSS
   against the budget.

## Evidence

Full numbers, per-clip diagnostics and logs: comment on
AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES; diagnostics artefacts under `/tmp/ah-soak/`
(`batch-1..5.diagnostics.json`) and
`capture-output/soak/soak-streamed2.diagnostics.json`.
data.title: In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget for long clips written outside the served repo root
